summary: 1. Focus strictly on immediate bodily, sensory, or visceral phenomena (e.g., pruning fingers, pineapple burning, leaking eyes) rather than distant engineering or abstract ecological chains. 2. Start the first sentence with an aggressive counter-intuitive claim or direct bodily confrontation (e.g., 'Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back') instead of setting up a hypothetical scenario ('Your car swerves off...'). 3. Immediately debunk a common misconception in sentence one using a contrast word like 'but' or 'not' (e.g., 'it is not because you are absorbing it like a sponge'). 4. Craft titles using action-driven or provocative phrasing ('Eat You Back', 'Secretly Leaking') rather than passive explanatory questions or technical jargon ('Heavy End Boxes', 'Lyme Disease Rates'). 5. Keep voiceover duration under 25 seconds of punchy pacing, eliminating cliché opener questions ('Ever noticed...?') that invite viewers to swipe away.
winning_hooks: State an active bodily disruption occurring right now ('Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it')
Debunk a universally accepted myth in the first 8 words ('Your fingers prune in water, but it is not because...')
Use extreme historical or visceral comparisons ('This shark is older than the United States' / 'Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back')
avoid: Cliché observational question openings like 'Ever noticed those tiny black dots...?'
Long situational story setups like 'You just smashed your elbow on a desk and now...'
Dry Wikipedia-style fact declarations like 'Honey is famous for being one of the only natural foods...'
next_experiment: Test Hook Frame: Compare a direct myth-busting contrast ('Topic X happens, but NOT because of Y') against an extreme personal confrontation ('Your body is currently doing X right now without you knowing') on the exact same topic.
